name: Bulova
tagline: New York's watch pioneer: radio ads, tuning forks and a chronograph on the Moon
summary: Bulova is one of America's oldest and best-known watch brands, founded in New York in 1875 and owned by Japan's Citizen Group since 2008. It is famous for broadcasting firsts, the Accutron tuning-fork watch, the Apollo 15 lunar chronograph and its high-frequency Precisionist quartz movements.
history:
Bulova began in 1875 when Bohemian immigrant Joseph Bulova opened a small jewelry shop on Maiden Lane in Manhattan. Over the following decades the company moved into watchmaking, building a factory in Switzerland in 1912 to standardise parts, and became a pioneer of mass-market marketing: in 1926 it aired the first nationwide radio time announcement, and in 1941 it broadcast what is widely cited as the first television commercial in the United States.

After the Second World War Bulova founded the Joseph Bulova School of Watchmaking to train disabled veterans. In 1960 it launched the Accutron, the first electronic watch regulated by a 360 Hz tuning fork, which became part of the American space programme. On 2 August 1971, Apollo 15 commander David Scott wore a Bulova chronograph on the lunar surface after his NASA-issued Omega's crystal came off, a watch that later sold at auction for more than $1.6 million.

The quartz era and changing ownership (Loews Corporation acquired control in 1979) saw Bulova refocus on accessible quartz watches. In 2008 Citizen Watch Co. bought Bulova for about $250 million. Under Citizen, Bulova introduced the 262 kHz Precisionist movement in 2010 and built a strong Archive Series of reissues such as the Lunar Pilot, Oceanographer 'Devil Diver', Computron and Super Seville. Accutron was spun off as a separate brand in 2020, while Bulova remains headquartered in New York.
knownFor: The Apollo 15 Lunar Pilot, Accutron heritage & 262 kHz Precisionist quartz

name: Accutron
tagline: The humming tuning-fork watch of the Space Age, reborn with electrostatic power
summary: Accutron began in 1960 as Bulova's revolutionary tuning-fork watch, the first electronic wristwatch to go mainstream and a fixture of the US space programme. Relaunched in 2020 as a standalone brand under Citizen, it now makes the Spaceview 2020 and DNA with the world's first electrostatic-powered movement.
history:
Accutron was born from the work of Swiss engineer Max Hetzel, who joined Bulova in the 1950s and developed a watch regulated by a 360 Hz tuning fork instead of a balance wheel. Launched in 1960, the Accutron 214 was guaranteed accurate to within a minute a month, far better than mechanical watches, and it famously hummed rather than ticked. The see-through Spaceview version, originally a display model for jewelers, became an icon.

Accutron's precision made it valuable to NASA: Accutron movements were used in spacecraft instruments and timers, and the Accutron Astronaut GMT was issued to test pilots. Quartz technology, arriving from 1969, made the tuning fork obsolete by the late 1970s, and the Accutron name became a line within Bulova's catalogue.

In 2020 Bulova, by then owned by Citizen, relaunched Accutron as a separate luxury brand. Its flagship Spaceview 2020 used a new electrostatic movement developed with Citizen, in which the wearer's motion spins turbines that generate electrostatic energy. Since then the brand has added the angular DNA, the Spaceview Evolution, Legacy reissues of 1960s–70s designs, a new Astronaut GMT and, most recently, a limited Spaceview 314 powered by a tuning-fork movement.
knownFor: The tuning-fork Accutron 214 & the electrostatic Spaceview 2020

name: Timex
tagline: It takes a licking and keeps on ticking: America's everyman watch since 1854
summary: Timex traces its roots to the Waterbury Clock Company, founded in Connecticut in 1854, and became the watch that put a timepiece on nearly every American wrist. Today Timex Group, still based in Connecticut, sells everything from $60 Weekenders and Ironman digitals to Marlin reissues and Giorgio Galli-designed automatics.
history:
Timex's story begins in 1854 in Waterbury, Connecticut, the 'Brass City', where the Waterbury Clock Company was founded as an offshoot of brass maker Benedict & Burnham. Its mass-production know-how made cheap, reliable timepieces possible, including the famous one-dollar Ingersoll 'Yankee' pocket watch of the 1890s, and Waterbury was also making wristwatches for soldiers by the First World War.

The company was nearly bankrupt in the Depression before Norwegian shipping magnate Thomas Olsen and engineer Joakim Lehmkuhl took control, reorganising it as the U.S. Time Corporation. In 1950 it launched the Timex brand: cheap, sturdy pin-lever watches sold in drugstores and promoted with TV 'torture tests' hosted by John Cameron Swayze, with the slogan 'It takes a licking and keeps on ticking.' By the 1960s about one in every two watches sold in the US was a Timex.

Timex survived the quartz and digital upheavals by moving into electronics, releasing the Ironman Triathlon sports watch in 1986, the Indiglo electroluminescent backlight in 1992 and the Data Link computer-linked watch with Microsoft in 1994. Now Timex Group B.V., still privately controlled by the Olsen family and headquartered in Middlebury, Connecticut, has recently won over enthusiasts with vintage reissues such as the Q Timex and Marlin, the Giorgio Galli S1 automatic and titanium Expedition and Marlin models.

name: Shinola
tagline: Detroit-built quartz and automatic watches that helped revive 'Made in America' cool
summary: Shinola is a Detroit-based lifestyle brand founded in 2011 by Fossil co-founder Tom Kartsotis's investment firm, best known for watches assembled in the city's Argonaut Building. Its Runwell, Canfield and Monster collections made it the most visible American watch assembler of the 2010s.
history:
Shinola was created in 2011 by Bedrock Manufacturing, the Texas investment firm of Fossil co-founder Tom Kartsotis. The company bought the name of a defunct American shoe-polish brand, remembered from the phrase 'you don't know shit from Shinola', and chose Detroit, a city struggling after the collapse of its manufacturing economy, as its home. A watch-assembly plant was built inside the College for Creative Studies' Argonaut Building, with Swiss movement specialist Ronda helping to train local workers.

The first watch, the Runwell, launched in 2013 and its limited edition sold out quickly. Shinola expanded rapidly into leather goods, bicycles, audio, jewelry and a hotel on Woodward Avenue, becoming a symbol of Detroit's revival. In 2016 the US Federal Trade Commission told the company to stop using the slogan 'Where American is Made', since many components were imported; Shinola now says its watches are 'Built in Detroit'.

Over time the company added its own Argonite quartz calibres assembled in-house, the Canfield sport line and automatic divers such as the Monster. By 2025 Shinola said it had assembled more than one million watches in Detroit, and after the US imposed steep tariffs on Swiss imports it ran a full-page newspaper ad inviting Swiss watchmakers to manufacture in Detroit.

name: Weiss Watch Company
tagline: A one-watchmaker revival of American field-watch manufacturing, now in Nashville
summary: Weiss is a small independent brand founded in 2013 by watchmaker Cameron Weiss, who hand-assembles field watches with a high proportion of American-made parts. Originally based in Los Angeles, the company moved to Nashville, Tennessee in 2020.
history:
Cameron Weiss trained as a watchmaker in the United States and Switzerland, earning WOSTEP certification, before founding Weiss Watch Company in Los Angeles in 2013 with his wife Whitney. His goal was to bring back small-scale American watchmaking, and his first Standard Issue Field Watches paired simple military-inspired dials with an increasing share of parts machined in the US.

The brand grew a loyal following as one of the few American companies making cases, dials and movement parts domestically rather than just assembling imported kits. Its watches were sold directly to customers and assembled, regulated and tested by hand in small batches.

In 2020 Weiss and his family moved the company to Nashville, citing the city's creative community and the local manufacturing base that serves the aerospace and automotive industries. They bought a building in the Wedgewood-Houston neighbourhood, and in 2024 opened a Nashville studio and boutique where collectors can see the workshop. The current lineup is built around 38 mm and 42 mm automatic Standard Issue Field Watches with matching date wheels, plus limited titanium and textured-dial editions. Weiss watches are sold mainly direct to customers, which lets the company keep production small and personal.

name: RGM
tagline: Pennsylvania's master watchmaker, building American movements by hand
summary: RGM Watch Co. was founded in 1992 by watchmaker Roland G. Murphy in Mount Joy, Pennsylvania. It is one of the only American companies to design and make its own movements, including the Caliber 801, the Caliber 20 and the Pennsylvania Tourbillon, and it does hand engine-turning and enamel work in-house.
history:
Roland G. Murphy studied watchmaking at the Bowman Technical School in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and at the WOSTEP school in Switzerland, then worked for Hamilton before founding RGM in 1992. Early RGM watches used Swiss movements in cases and dials designed in Pennsylvania, and the brand became known for special pieces for railway enthusiasts and military units, such as the Corps of Engineers watches.

Murphy's larger ambition was to revive American movement-making. In 2007 RGM completed the Caliber 801, a manual-wind movement produced in-house, making it the first American company in decades to make its own mechanical movement in series. It was followed by the Pennsylvania Tourbillon and, for the brand's 20th anniversary, the Caliber 20, whose motor barrel and moonphase recall the best American railroad pocket watches.

RGM also invested in rose-engine and straight-line engine-turning machines to make guilloché dials by hand, and offers Grand Feu enamel dials. Still a small, independent family workshop in Mount Joy, the company also restores vintage watches and makes pieces to order, from the Swiss-powered Model 151 pilot's watch to high-end Caliber 801 pieces.

name: Vortic
tagline: Antique American pocket-watch movements reborn as Colorado-built wristwatches
summary: Vortic Watch Company, founded in 2013 in Fort Collins, Colorado, turns restored antique American pocket-watch movements into one-of-a-kind wristwatches. It is also known for winning a landmark trademark case brought by Swatch Group's Hamilton.
history:
Vortic was founded in 2013 by R.T. Custer and Tyler Wolfe, who met as students and wanted to build watches in the United States. Their idea was to rescue movements from antique American pocket watches made by companies such as Elgin, Waltham, Illinois and Hamilton, restore them and fit them into new wristwatch cases. A Kickstarter campaign in 2014 raised about $41,000 and launched the business in Fort Collins.

In 2015 Hamilton, owned by Swatch Group, sued Vortic and Custer personally, alleging counterfeiting and trademark infringement because some restored movements bore the Hamilton name. After a five-year fight, a US federal judge ruled in Vortic's favour on all counts in September 2020, affirming the right to restore and resell antique watches with their original markings. The case became a notable precedent for upcycling.

Vortic makes a few hundred watches a year, each unique, in series named after the cities of the original makers, plus an annual Military Edition built around US Army Air Corps pocket watches, and it offers conversions of customers' heirloom watches. It also launched the sister brand Colorado Watch Company. In June 2025 Custer suffered a major stroke; his wife Lindsay Roselle has run the company as interim CEO during his recovery.

name: Waltham
tagline: America's first watch factory, inventor of mass production, reborn in Switzerland
summary: The Waltham Watch Company, founded in 1850 in Massachusetts, pioneered the 'American System' of making watches with interchangeable machine-made parts and produced around 40 million timepieces before its US factory closed in 1957. The brand lives on through its Swiss offshoot, now based in Mendrisio, which makes modern mechanical watches such as the Field & Marine Dual Time.
history:
Waltham began in 1850 when Aaron Lufkin Dennison, with Edward Howard and David Davis, set out to make watches by machine rather than by hand. After starting near Boston, the company moved in 1854 to Waltham, Massachusetts, on the Charles River. There it perfected what became known as the American System of Watch Manufacturing, using precision machinery to make interchangeable parts. The approach shocked Swiss makers when Waltham's watches beat them at the 1876 Philadelphia Centennial Exhibition.

Waltham became one of the largest watchmakers in the world. Its pocket watches, from the affordable William Ellery, the model Abraham Lincoln owned, to the railroad-grade Vanguard and Crescent Street, set the standard for American railways. It made wristwatches for soldiers in the First World War, aircraft clocks and, during the Second World War, military watches such as the A-11 and A-17 alongside Elgin and Bulova.

After the war, cheap imports and management problems pushed Waltham into bankruptcy in 1949, and US watch production ended in 1957. A Swiss subsidiary, Waltham International SA, created in 1954, kept the trademark outside North America. Italian-American businessman Antonio DiBenedetto took majority control in 2011, and the Swiss-made brand, now headquartered in Mendrisio, relaunched with pilot's watches such as the Aeronaval line and, more recently, the Field & Marine Dual Time based on a 1918 waterproof design. The original factory buildings are preserved as a historic district, and the company's archives are held at Harvard Business School.

name: Elgin
tagline: Illinois giant that built half of America's pocket watches
summary: The Elgin National Watch Company, founded in 1864, ran the world's largest watchmaking complex in Elgin, Illinois, and made about half of all pocket watches produced in the United States. US manufacturing ended in 1968; the Elgin name has since been sold several times and is now used by MZ Berger on inexpensive fashion watches with no link to the original company.
history:
The National Watch Company was founded in Chicago in 1864 by a group of businessmen led by former Chicago mayor Benjamin W. Raymond, and it built its factory in the town of Elgin, Illinois. Its first watch, the B.W. Raymond, appeared in 1867. The company was renamed the Elgin National Watch Company in 1874, adopting the name its customers already used.

Elgin grew into a giant. By the 1920s its Elgin plant covered more than 21 acres and employed over 4,000 people, and the company eventually produced roughly half of all pocket watches made in the US. It supplied railroad-grade models, built the Elgin Observatory in 1910 to set time precisely, and turned to military production during the Second World War, making watches and precision instruments for US forces. Its Lord Elgin line became a well-known American wristwatch brand in the mid-20th century.

Foreign competition and changing tastes hit hard after the war. The original Plant No. 1 closed in 1964, and all US watch manufacturing ended in 1968. The Elgin name was sold and resold, and the current owner, MZ Berger & Co., uses it on affordable imported watches. Collectors, however, value original Elgin pocket watches and wristwatches, and many surviving movements are now rebuilt into wristwatches by companies such as Vortic.

name: Benrus
tagline: Military-issue American watch brand worn by Steve McQueen, revived in New York
summary: Benrus was founded in New York in 1921 by the Lazrus brothers and became one of America's largest watch companies, known for military watches such as the DTU-2A/P and the Type I and Type II. Revived after a 2018 recapitalisation, it now makes Swiss-made reissues of its military and civilian classics from New York.
history:
Benjamin, Oscar and Ralph Lazrus, immigrants from Romania, founded Benrus in Manhattan in 1921, combining Benjamin's first name with the family surname. The company grew quickly by importing Swiss movements and casing them in the US, and by the mid-century it was among the country's largest watch brands, headquartered at the Hippodrome building on Sixth Avenue.

Benrus is best remembered for its military work. It supplied the US armed forces with the DTU-2A/P field watch from 1964 and, in the 1970s, the rugged Type I and Type II dive-style watches for special operations units. Its civilian #3061 version of a military design became famous when Steve McQueen wore it in the 1968 film Bullitt, and the Sky Chief chronograph was a popular pilot's watch.

The quartz era and financial trouble ended the original business in the late 1970s, and the name passed through several owners. In 2018 a private investment group led by lawyer Michael Sweeney acquired the brand, and it relaunched with a team of industry veterans, a facility in La Chaux-de-Fonds and a new headquarters back at the Hippodrome in New York. Today's Swiss-made collection revives the DTU, Type I, Type II, #3061 and Sky Chief alongside the carbon-and-titanium Type 3X.

name: Ball Watch
tagline: Railroad-standard accuracy since 1891, lit by self-powered tritium tubes
summary: Ball Watch Company was founded in Cleveland in 1891 by Webb C. Ball, whose railroad timekeeping standards made American trains safer. Now Swiss-based in La Chaux-de-Fonds and owned by Hong Kong's Asia Commercial Holdings, it makes rugged mechanical watches lit by tritium gas tubes.
history:
Webb C. Ball was a Cleveland jeweler when, after a deadly train collision at Kipton, Ohio, in April 1891 was blamed on an unreliable watch, he was appointed chief time inspector for the Lake Shore railroad lines. He introduced the General Railroad Timepiece Standards, which required watches to meet strict accuracy and design rules, along with regular inspection by certified watchmakers. The system spread across roughly 125,000 miles of US railways, and 'Ball time' became a byword for accuracy.

Ball's company did not make movements itself: it bought them from makers such as Waltham, Hamilton and Elgin, and sold Ball-standard watches to railroad men. The business remained in the family for decades, supplying railroads until the mid-20th century.

In the 1990s the brand was reborn around rugged sports watches for demanding conditions. It was acquired from the Ball family around 2000 by private investors, moved its international headquarters to La Chaux-de-Fonds in Switzerland and adopted the motto 'Accuracy under adverse conditions'. Every modern Ball uses self-powered micro gas tubes (tritium) for constant illumination, and the brand developed shock-protection and anti-magnetic systems for lines such as the Engineer, Engineer Hydrocarbon, Roadmaster, Trainmaster and Fireman. Today the company is owned by Hong Kong-based Asia Commercial Holdings.

name: Invicta
tagline: Swiss-born in 1837, reborn in Florida as the king of big, bold, budget watches
summary: Invicta was founded in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1837 by Raphael Picard and is now run from Hollywood, Florida, by the Lalo family. It is known for huge catalogues of inexpensive, oversized watches sold largely through TV shopping and online, and above all for the Pro Diver.
history:
Raphael Picard founded Invicta in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1837 with the aim of making good Swiss watches at prices a broad public could afford; the name is Latin for 'invincible'. The company won a gold medal at the 1914 Swiss National Exhibition in Bern and supplied watches to Allied forces during the Second World War.

Like much of the Swiss industry, Invicta nearly disappeared in the quartz crisis, and its parent company went bankrupt in 1982. In 1991 Eyal Lalo, whose family had been involved in distributing Invicta, acquired the brand and rebuilt it in the United States. Under the Lalo family, Invicta Watch Group moved its headquarters to Hollywood, Florida, and became famous for its sheer output, reportedly designing around 1,500 new models a year, mostly with Japanese movements, and selling them heavily through TV shopping channels and online at deep discounts from high list prices.

The Pro Diver, particularly the automatic 8926OB with a Seiko NH35 movement, became one of the best-selling watches on Amazon and a popular entry point for new collectors. Invicta bought the Swiss brand Glycine in 2016 and filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023 to restructure its retail operations, while continuing to sell watches worldwide.

name: Fossil
tagline: Texas-born fashion-watch giant behind Fossil, Skagen and dozens of licensed labels
summary: Fossil was founded in 1984 by Tom Kartsotis in Texas and grew into Fossil Group, one of the world's largest makers of fashion watches, both its own brands and licences such as Michael Kors, Armani Exchange and Diesel. After a costly move into smartwatches, it left that market in 2024 and has been restructuring its business.
history:
Tom Kartsotis founded Overseas Products International in Dallas in 1984, importing inexpensive watches from Asia; the Fossil brand's name came from a nickname for his father. With retro-styled designs, strong branding and distinctive tin packaging, Fossil became a hit in American department stores, and brother Kosta Kartsotis joined to lead its growth. The company went public in 1993 and later renamed itself Fossil Group.

Fossil expanded by buying brands such as Zodiac, Michele and Skagen, and by manufacturing licensed watches for fashion houses including Emporio Armani, Diesel, DKNY and Michael Kors, whose watch boom in the early 2010s drove revenue to record highs. Headquartered in Richardson, Texas, it became one of the largest watch companies outside Switzerland and Japan.

As smartphones cut into fashion-watch demand, Fossil bought wearables start-up Misfit for $260 million in 2015 and produced Wear OS smartwatches and hybrid watches for many of its brands; in 2019 it sold some smartwatch technology to Google. Sales kept falling, and in January 2024 the company said it would leave the smartwatch business. Franco Fogliato became CEO in September 2024, 2024 revenue was about $1.14 billion, and in 2025 the group went through a debt restructuring that included UK proceedings recognised in the US under Chapter 15.

name: Nixon
tagline: Surf-and-skate watch brand from Southern California
summary: Nixon was founded in 1997 in Encinitas, California, by Andy Laats and Chad DiNenna to make watches and accessories for the surf, skate and snow crowd. Now based in Carlsbad and co-owned by its founders, Billabong and Trilantic Capital, it is known for models such as the Time Teller and 51-30.
history:
Andy Laats and Chad DiNenna founded Nixon in Encinitas, California, in 1997, aiming to make 'custom built' watches for the action-sports community rather than repurposed fashion pieces. Early models such as the Time Teller and chunky dive and chronograph watches spread through surf and skate shops and team riders.

The brand grew fast, adding bags, headphones and apparel, and in 2006 Australian surf group Billabong bought it for about $55 million plus later payments. In 2012 the founders took control again in a joint venture with Trilantic Capital Partners, returning Nixon to independence; it is now co-owned by Billabong, Trilantic, Laats and DiNenna.

Nixon became known for big, colourful watches such as the 51-30 chronograph, the Sentry, the tide-reading Base and the Regulus digital, and for pop-culture collaborations with Star Wars, Metallica and others. It sells in more than 90 countries and now works mainly through retail partners and its own online store, from headquarters in Carlsbad, California. The brand's name and early marketing leaned on its outsider identity, and its watches were designed to be tough enough for surfing, skating and snowboarding while standing out in bold colours and oversized cases. Nixon's catalogue also covers tide watches for surfers and simple digital models, and it has used limited collaborations to reach music and film fans.

name: MVMT
tagline: The crowdfunded, Instagram-built watch brand for millennials
summary: MVMT (pronounced 'movement') was founded in Los Angeles in 2013 by college dropouts Jake Kassan and Kramer LaPlante, who raised money on Indiegogo and sold minimalist watches directly online through social media. Movado Group bought it in 2018 for more than $100 million.
history:
Jake Kassan and Kramer LaPlante started MVMT in Los Angeles in June 2013 with the idea of selling stylish, minimalist watches for about $100, far below designer brands. Two Indiegogo campaigns raised more than $290,000, and the pair built the business almost entirely online, using Instagram influencers and Facebook advertising to reach young buyers.

The approach worked: MVMT passed 600,000 watches sold by the end of 2016, expanded into sunglasses and jewelry, and described itself as 'a watch brand by and for millennials'. In 2017 most of its customers were under 34.

In August 2018 Movado Group bought MVMT for more than $100 million, with further payments tied to performance, and the founders later left. Under Movado the brand has broadened its range to include chronographs, solar and automatic divers such as the Cali Diver GMT, while keeping its direct-to-consumer model from its Los Angeles base. MVMT's early watches, like the Classic and the Chrono, had clean dials and quartz movements, and the brand's success inspired a wave of similar online-first watch start-ups. Its marketing relied heavily on travel and lifestyle imagery rather than watchmaking heritage.

name: Oak & Oscar
tagline: Chicago microbrand making Swiss-powered field, GMT and chronograph watches
summary: Oak & Oscar is an independent Chicago watch company founded in 2015 by Chase Fancher and named after his dog Oscar. Its well-finished Swiss-powered watches, named after figures and places linked to Chicago and the outdoors, have made it one of the most respected American microbrands.
history:
Chase Fancher, a Chicago watch enthusiast, launched Oak & Oscar in 2015. The first watch, the Burnham, was a Swiss automatic field watch named after Daniel Burnham, the architect and planner behind much of Chicago's layout, and it established the brand's style: sandwich dials, orange accents and details such as canvas-and-leather watch wallets.

The brand followed with limited runs such as the Sandford diver and the Jackson flyback chronograph, which sold out quickly, and built a loyal owner community with events and Chicago-themed limited editions, including collaborations with Few Spirits and the US Secret Service.

The core range now consists of the 38 mm Olmsted field watch, named after landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted, the Humboldt GMT with a ceramic 24-hour bezel and anti-magnetic Faraday cage, and the Atwood, a manually wound column-wheel flyback chronograph using a Sellita AMT movement. An 'Experimental Series' has explored in-house finishing and heat-treated components made at the company's Chicago headquarters. The company assembles and tests its watches in small batches and has become known for strong customer relationships, including owners' weekends and events for its community of collectors.

name: Lorier
tagline: Husband-and-wife microbrand making vintage-style watches at under $1,000
summary: Lorier is a New York-based microbrand founded by Lauren and Mike Tsai that makes 36–39 mm vintage-inspired dive, field, dress and GMT watches with Miyota movements. Its compact cases, domed crystals and fair pricing have made it an enthusiast favourite.
history:
Lorier was started by husband-and-wife team Lauren and Mike Tsai in New York, with the goal of making the kind of mid-century-inspired watches they loved at an accessible price. The brand launched with the Neptune dive watch and quickly became known for modest case sizes, vintage-style domed crystals and gilt details, a contrast to the oversized watches common among microbrands at the time.

The range grew to include the Falcon field watch, with a 3-6-9 dial and broad-arrow hands, the Astra dress-sport watch and the Hyperion GMT, powered by a Miyota 9075 with an independently adjustable local hour hand. Lorier sells directly online, in batches, keeping prices below $1,000.

Recent updates to the core collection added sapphire crystals and, on divers and GMTs, sapphire bezel inserts, improving durability while keeping the vintage look. The company trades as Studio Lorier with the slogan 'Legacy in Action'. Lorier's designs draw on dive, field and travel watches from the 1950s to the 1970s, reinterpreted with modern parts. Its watches are typically released in limited batches that sell directly to customers, and the brand has become a common recommendation for buyers seeking vintage character without vintage fragility.

name: Halios
tagline: Vancouver's cult one-man microbrand of dive and sport watches
summary: Halios is a small Vancouver brand founded by Jason Lim that makes limited batches of dive and sport watches such as the Seaforth, Delfin, Fairwind and Universa. Its watches routinely sell out through pre-orders and are highly regarded for design and finishing at their price.
history:
Jason Lim founded Halios in Vancouver, British Columbia, as a passion project, releasing small batches of dive watches designed by himself and produced with Swiss and Asian suppliers. Early models such as the Holotype and Puck established a reputation for clean, tool-like design and careful detailing.

The brand's popularity grew with the Delfin, a 1960s-style skin diver, the Tropik, and above all the Seaforth, a compact diver offered with fixed or rotating bezels and many dial colours, including sunburst and pastel shades. Releases are made to order in limited runs, and demand has consistently exceeded supply, earning Halios a cult following among collectors.

More recent designs include the Fairwind, a slim sports watch with an integrated feel, and the Universa, a 38 mm sport-dress watch whose latest version uses galvanically treated or vitreous enamel dials. The fourth-generation Seaforth moved to titanium with a Sellita movement, continuing Halios's approach of small, carefully planned production. Lim handles the design work himself and deliberately keeps the brand small, which is part of its appeal to collectors. Halios watches are known for high-quality dials, crisp case finishing and well-judged proportions, and many enthusiasts consider the brand one of the pioneers of the modern microbrand movement.

name: Marathon
tagline: Canadian family firm supplying Swiss-made issue watches to the US military
summary: Marathon is a fourth-generation family company, designed in Canada and manufactured in La Chaux-de-Fonds, that has supplied military watches since the Second World War. Its tritium-lit Search and Rescue divers and Navigators are official issue for the US armed forces and other governments.
history:
Marathon's roots go back to 1904, when the Wein family founded Weinstrum Watch in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland. In 1939 Morris Wein established the Marathon Watch Company, and from 1941 it supplied watches to the Allied forces during the Second World War. The family settled in Canada, where the company is based, while its watches continue to be made in Switzerland.

Marathon became a key supplier of military timepieces. It builds watches to the US military standard MIL-PRF-46374G and to Canadian government specifications for search-and-rescue work, and has been a leading supplier of issue watches to the US armed forces. Its designs, such as the plastic-cased Navigator pilot's watch and the steel Search and Rescue (SAR) divers, are illuminated with tritium gas tubes so they glow continuously without charging.

While its watches are issued to soldiers, sailors and aircrew, Marathon also sells them to civilians, and military-watch enthusiasts value them for their authenticity and toughness. The line-up includes the 41 mm GSAR automatic diver, the 46 mm JSAR and JDD, the CSAR automatic chronograph, the Navigator and General Purpose field watches. The business remains owned and run by the Wein family, now in its fourth generation.

name: Brew
tagline: New York microbrand of 1970s-style chronographs inspired by espresso
summary: Brew Watch Co. was founded in New York by industrial designer Jonathan Ferrer, who draws on 1970s design and coffee culture for compact, colourful watches. Its 36 mm Metric chronograph is one of the best-known microbrand designs of recent years.
history:
Jonathan Ferrer, an industrial designer in New York, started Brew around 2015 with a Kickstarter-funded first watch inspired by espresso machines and the rituals of coffee culture. His designs borrow the cushion cases and bold colours of 1970s watches, and they keep sizes small at a time when many brands were making larger watches.

The Retrograph chronograph was designed to time an espresso shot, with its scale highlighting the 25–35 second extraction window. The 36 mm Metric followed with a brushed-and-polished cushion case and many colourways, from the Retro dial to titanium, PVD and textured 'Bloom' versions, and it earned coverage from Hodinkee, Bloomberg and The New York Times.

Brew has since added the Super Metric in brighter colours, the 30 mm automatic Metric Lite and the Digital Blend, which pairs analog time with an LED espresso-shot timer, while continuing to release limited editions and collaborations. Brew watches are designed in New York and sold mostly online, with frequent small-batch colourways that sell quickly. The brand's playful approach, mixing industrial design with coffee culture, has helped it stand out among microbrands and attract buyers who are new to watches.

name: Nodus
tagline: Los Angeles microbrand obsessed with engineering details
summary: Nodus Watches was founded in Los Angeles in 2017 by Cullen Chen and Wes Kasper. It designs and assembles tool watches in LA, such as the Sector, Contrail and Unity, and is known for engineering touches like its own crown and bezel systems and the Intersect watch fair.
history:
Cullen Chen and Wes Kasper, two young Los Angeles watch enthusiasts, started Nodus in 2017 with the Trieste dive watch. From the start they did final assembly, regulation and testing in their own Los Angeles workshop, and they described the company as a watch research and design studio rather than just a brand.

Nodus built a reputation for engineering details at affordable prices, including its own crown tubes, bezel click mechanisms and crystal shapes. Models such as the Contrail, a slim travel watch with a Miyota 9075 GMT movement, and the Sector, a family of field, sport and GMT watches with a fast-set jumping GMT hand, sold out in batches.

In 2021 Nodus founded Intersect, a watch-industry gathering that became a joint venture with Formex and Jack Mason, and it runs a Design Lab platform for collaborative designs. Recent releases include the Sector II series with stone dials, full titanium bracelets, the Obscura II and the 36.5 mm Unity with vitreous dials. The founders have kept prices accessible while focusing on robust construction, and most releases are made in limited batches that sell directly to customers.

name: Apple (Apple Watch)
tagline: The world's best-selling watch, which turned the wrist into a health computer
summary: Apple entered watches in 2015 with the Apple Watch, which quickly became the world's best-selling watch of any kind. Built around health and fitness sensing, it now spans the Series, the rugged Ultra and the affordable SE, plus Hermès editions.
history:
Apple, founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne in California, announced the Apple Watch in September 2014 and released it in April 2015. The first generation was pitched partly as a luxury object, with an 18-carat gold Edition priced at more than $10,000, and it introduced the Digital Crown as a way to navigate a tiny touchscreen. A partnership with Hermès brought leather straps and branded faces.

Apple soon refocused the watch on fitness and health. Series 2 added GPS and swim-proofing, Series 3 cellular connectivity, and Series 4 in 2018 an electrical heart sensor for ECG readings, cleared by the US FDA, along with fall detection. Later models added blood-oxygen sensing, temperature sensing and sleep-apnea notifications, and the watch has been credited with alerting users to heart problems.

The Apple Watch Ultra of 2022 added a 49 mm titanium case, an orange Action button and dive-computer features, and the lower-priced SE line broadened the audience. By the late 2010s Apple was shipping more watches each year than the entire Swiss watch industry. In 2026 the range comprises the Series 12 in aluminium, titanium and ceramic, the Ultra 4 with satellite messaging, and the SE 3.

name: Garmin
tagline: GPS pioneer turned king of sports and adventure smartwatches
summary: Garmin was founded in Kansas in 1989 by Gary Burrell and Min Kao and made its name in GPS navigation before becoming a leader in GPS sports watches. Its fēnix, Forerunner, Instinct and Venu lines lead the premium outdoor and fitness smartwatch market.
history:
Gary Burrell and Min Kao founded the company in 1989 in Lenexa, Kansas, as ProNav, later renaming it Garmin from their first names. Its early GPS receivers were used by aviators, sailors and the US military, and in the 2000s its car satnavs became a mass-market hit.

In 2003 Garmin launched the Forerunner 201, the first wrist-worn GPS training device for runners, creating a new category. As smartphones undercut car navigation, fitness and outdoor watches became central to Garmin's growth: the Forerunner for runners, the fēnix multisport adventure watch, the rugged Instinct and the lifestyle-focused Venu, plus the MARQ luxury line and specialist aviation, diving and marine watches.

Garmin bought DeLorme in 2016, adding the satellite messaging now built into some watches, and fitness-analytics firm Firstbeat in 2020. It became the leader in premium smartwatches costing over $500, known for long battery life, solar charging and detailed training metrics. Legally domiciled in Schaffhausen, Switzerland, since 2010 but operated from Olathe, Kansas, Garmin reported revenue of about $7.25 billion in 2025 with around 23,000 employees. Garmin designs its own watch software and sensors, and much of its manufacturing is done in its own facilities in Taiwan.

name: Samsung (Galaxy Watch)
tagline: Android's leading smartwatch, famous for its rotating bezel
summary: Samsung Electronics has made smartwatches since the 2013 Galaxy Gear, and its Galaxy Watch line is the leading watch for Android users. Recent models run Wear OS, and the line includes the rotating-bezel Classic and the titanium Galaxy Watch Ultra.
history:
Samsung Electronics, founded in 1969 as part of the Samsung group started by Lee Byung-chul, launched its first smartwatch, the Galaxy Gear, in 2013 alongside the Galaxy Note 3. Early Gear models used Android and then Samsung's own Tizen system, and the 2015 Gear S2 introduced a rotating bezel for navigating the round screen, a feature that became a hallmark.

The line was renamed Galaxy Watch in 2018, and in 2021 Samsung and Google merged their efforts into the Wear OS platform, with the Galaxy Watch4 as the first Samsung watch to run it. Samsung added body-composition analysis, ECG and blood-pressure features (in supported markets), and sleep coaching.

The 2024 Galaxy Watch Ultra introduced a titanium cushion-shaped case with 10 ATM water resistance aimed at outdoor athletes. The current range includes the Galaxy Watch9, the Galaxy Watch8 Classic with its rotating bezel, and the Galaxy Watch Ultra2, sold alongside Samsung's Galaxy phones from its headquarters in Suwon, South Korea. Galaxy Watches are designed to work best with Samsung's Galaxy phones, and features such as ECG and blood-pressure monitoring depend on regional approvals. The line is one of the best-selling smartwatches in the world outside the Apple ecosystem.

name: Google (Pixel Watch / Fitbit)
tagline: Google's round Wear OS smartwatch, powered by Fitbit health tracking
summary: Google makes the Pixel Watch and owns Fitbit, the fitness-tracker pioneer it acquired in 2021. The domed, round Pixel Watch launched in 2022 and combines Wear OS with Fitbit's health and sleep tracking.
history:
Fitbit was founded in 2007 by James Park and Eric Friedman in San Francisco and popularised the clip-on and wrist-worn step counter. It went public in 2015, bought smartwatch start-up Pebble's software assets in 2016 and launched smartwatches such as the Ionic, Versa and Sense.

Google, founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, had developed the Android Wear (later Wear OS) platform in 2014 for other manufacturers' watches. It announced a $2.1 billion deal for Fitbit in 2019, which closed in January 2021 after regulatory review, and in 2021 merged its smartwatch platform efforts with Samsung.

The first Google Pixel Watch launched in October 2022 with a round, domed design and Fitbit health features built in. Later generations added a larger 45 mm size, better battery life and satellite SOS, and in 2025 the Pixel Watch 4 was followed in 2026 by the Pixel Watch 5. Google continues to sell Fitbit trackers such as the Charge 6 alongside the Pixel Watch from its headquarters in Mountain View, California. The Pixel Watch is designed to work with Android phones and Google services, and many health features rely on a Fitbit subscription.

name: Huawei
tagline: Chinese tech giant making long-battery, elegantly styled smartwatches
summary: Huawei, the Shenzhen-based technology group founded in 1987, is one of the world's largest wearables makers. Its Watch GT line is known for classic round designs and battery life measured in weeks, and it also makes premium titanium and blood-pressure-measuring watches.
history:
Ren Zhengfei founded Huawei in Shenzhen in 1987 as a telecom-equipment reseller, and it grew into one of the world's largest makers of networking gear and smartphones. The company describes itself as employee-owned through a union shareholding scheme.

Huawei's first smartwatch, the round Huawei Watch, arrived in 2015 running Android Wear, and the Watch GT of 2018 switched to Huawei's own lightweight software to achieve battery life of up to two weeks, which became its hallmark. After US sanctions in 2019 cut off access to Google services, Huawei moved its watches to its own HarmonyOS and continued to grow, especially in China, Europe and the Middle East.

Huawei's range now spans the Watch GT series with traditional-looking cases, the premium Watch Ultimate in Liquidmetal and titanium, the Watch Fit fitness line, and the Watch D series, which uses a tiny built-in air pump to take cuff-style blood-pressure readings. Current models include the Watch GT 7 Pro, the Watch 6 Pro and the Watch D3. Huawei watches are not generally sold in the United States. In China, Huawei is among the leading sellers of wearables, and its watches are also popular in Europe and the Middle East.

name: Withings
tagline: French health-tech firm whose hybrid watches hide medical sensors behind real hands
summary: Withings, founded in 2008 near Paris, makes connected health devices and is best known in watches for hybrid smartwatches that look like classic analog watches. Its Activité and ScanWatch lines add step counting, heart-rhythm and blood-oxygen sensing behind physical hands.
history:
Éric Carreel, Cédric Hutchings and Fred Potter founded Withings in June 2008 in Issy-les-Moulineaux, just outside Paris. Its first hit was a Wi-Fi bathroom scale, followed by connected blood-pressure monitors, thermometers and sleep trackers.

In 2014 Withings launched the Activité, a Swiss-made analog watch with a hidden activity tracker and a sub-dial showing progress toward a step goal; it was described as the first smartwatch to look like a traditional wristwatch. Nokia bought the company in 2016 and rebranded its products under the Nokia name, but in 2018 co-founder Éric Carreel bought it back and restored the Withings brand.

Independent again, Withings launched the ScanWatch in 2020, a hybrid watch with a small digital screen and sensors for ECG and blood-oxygen readings aimed at detecting atrial fibrillation and signs of sleep apnoea. It has since added the ScanWatch 2 with temperature sensing (2023), the cheaper ScanWatch Light (2024) and the dive-style ScanWatch Nova, alongside devices such as ECG-equipped smart scales and a home urine analyser. Several Withings devices have received medical clearances, reflecting the company's focus on health data rather than apps and notifications.
